0.content:
Alice, Klee's mother and a Hexenzirkel mage, met Prune in Nod-Krai when she spotted her reading a pirated travel guide by the road. Prune said the author seemed self-absorbed, with "troubling tendencies" between the lines. Alice then kept ambushing her with absurd questions and debates, rewarding each of Prune's "wins" with prizes. When Descartes had nearly faded away, she cackled like a stage villain, snapped her fingers and announced she had taken him: Prune was now the "Witch Hunter" and must beat every mage, starting with clues from Klee in Mondstadt. Prune screamed after her and set off. In Mondstadt Prune posted notices denouncing the witch "A" as an intellectual bully who abducts "soul companions". Prune calls her a show-off with a hollowed-out hat and the wickedest witch of all.

Alice's own account, given to the Traveler during the limited-time Phantasmal Pals event (6.6): she never took Descartes. Prune's innocence was buckling under a child's attempt to step into the adult world, so Alice invented a quest and chose Mondstadt because "the seeds of spirit and imagination are best nurtured by the soil of freedom", and because Klee needed a playmate. Alice also wrote Klee that a big sister named Prune would make a perfect friend. Nicole reports Alice saying she did it "because it makes life more entertaining".

1.content:
Descartes is Prune's imaginary friend: a small dog with indigo and violet markings, a brainy brow and deep dark eyes. He took shape when she, finished with a book too heavy for her age and with no one to talk to, began explaining it to the empty air. She named him after looking for something worthy of "intellectual inquiry". They debate silently ("speech... is far too inefficient") and he points out flaws in her deductions with a glance. In Nasha Town she discussed whether the world is a reflection in a puddle with him, worrying passers-by. He began to fade as Prune grew up too fast; Alice "took" him just before he vanished.

In the limited-time event The Magic That Never Fails (6.6), after Prune accepted Klee's invitation to the Little Hexenzirkel, Descartes reappeared, and Alice's magic briefly let everyone see all the imaginary friends (Dodoco, Yuegui, Tuantuan, a finch, Sayu's mujina Gena) together. Descartes explained the "long story", and Prune learned she had been tricked. She did not regret coming. In Kaeya's plan Descartes was to become heavy cavalry with a riding licence.

2.content:
Prune approached Klee to extract intel on her mother and quickly abandoned an outright abduction plan as beneath a real hunter. Klee instead kept turning up with snacks and toys: crystalfly catching, puddle jumping with Mini Durin, drawing on walls, rolling down Windrise's slopes and long introductions to every Dodoco. "Operation Bake-and-Grill" (cookies for answers) failed completely; Klee's "secret base" was "in the heart". Prune filed one drawing, "Prune and Klee Blow Up Fish Together", in her dossier. The two drew bomb-defusal doodles around Millhaven, then had to scrub the crayon off before being sent to confinement; Klee offered to blow up the wall instead. Klee calls Prune "the best" and plans to take her fish blasting, to Dragonspine and to Simulanka.

In her Witch's Homework quest Prune defended Klee passionately: nurture over nature, Klee accepts confinement, the latest fish blasting was her mother's idea, and above all Klee is kind and thinks well even of "her mother's sworn enemy". Klee's 2026 birthday mail says they still play "Answer or You're Toast", where answers earn toasted snacks, and that Prune baked Midsommar Tortes from her hometown.

3.content:
During the limited-time 6.6 flagship event Phantasmal Pals, Prune followed rumours of a witch and a rampaging Forest Boar to Chinju Forest in Inazuma, where she met the Traveler and Paimon and pretended to be Alice's friend. Her bell led them to Klee and the Little Hexenzirkel, a club Klee founded with Yaoyao, Qiqi and Sayu (Paimon joined on the spot). Prune refused to join ("I stopped playing pretend a long time ago") but helped them, and the Yumekui-Baku Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (the "Dough King"), cure the imaginary boar Popcorn. Afterwards she broke down, confessed she was a Witch Hunter, and cried while the little witches held her hands. Persuaded that the Little Hexenzirkel did not exist when Alice set her challenge, she joined, mortified, with the introduction-magic titles "Witch Hunter", "The Only Sane One in a Cruel World (Self-Proclaimed)" and "A Kid Nonetheless". Descartes returned at once.

She later admitted the club changed her: for once she feels needed and cared for, not on the outside looking in, and anyone who threatens it will "have to go through" her. She plans for it to become the strongest organisation in Teyvat and replace Alice's generation with a new order of justice, kindness and friendship.

4.comment: Prune: Witchlure Bell and Hexhunter Oathhammer
4.content:
After Descartes was "taken", Prune reviewed every prize Alice had ever given her and picked the two most promising. The bell ("When the bell rings, a witch might appear") was really an old Hexenzirkel tea-party bell; the "might" meant attendance was optional. It never guarantees a witch but never fails to start an adventure; in practice it floats, rings at "localised abnormal magical fluctuations", and once summoned a Whopperflower. The hammer was a sculpting tool Alice meant to give Nicole, who declined it politely ("My hobby is sculpting, not construction and demolition"). Prune renamed both after "very logical and practical" modifications, and Aino gave them a more industrial look.

Her modifications, including a longer handle for leverage, made the hammer too heavy to lift until her Vision arrived. In Inazuma she taught Sayu to use it as stilts. Alice once spoke to the Traveler through the floating bell.

5.comment: Prune: A Proposition Beyond Refutation (Witch's Homework)
5.content:
Prune's permanent Witch's Homework quest (6.6). The Traveler found Alice's taunt in the witch's dictionary; Prune's sarcastic "Look at me, I'm an idiot" was replayed by phonographs all over the plaza, and she smashed several with her hammer. Alice then hosted a debate in a magical copy of the Opera Epiclese, with the Traveler as judge and Paimon in the box seats, on the topic "Klee Is a Bad Kid". Prune argued that conduct is not inherited, that Klee accepts her punishments, that the last fish blasting was Alice's idea, that Klee is cute and kind, and that the real "Bad Kid-ult" was Alice. Alice conceded happily, called it a test of Prune's feelings for Klee, granted a "Witch's Blessing" and vanished again.

The act's description in The Little Witch's Dictionary jokes that the hunter fell into the witch's trap, made friends with Dodocos in a flowery meadow, and fell into the next trap, asking "Just who is the hunter here?"

6.content: Alice told Prune that "Witch B" was called "Megistus", leaving off the "Tris". In Dornman Port, Prune posted glow-in-the-dark notices calling the astrologist living there "B", accusing her of spending her money on forbidden age-reversal alchemy and demanding she reveal her associates. Mona replied in writing that it was her rarely used family home, that "Megistus" is a title and that the astrologist who dueled Alice was her master. Mona reported her; the Knights picked up the child "yelling about the 'filth of the adult world'" as she tried to pick the lock, and Albedo collected her. Prune later apologised and Mona accepted. She also tried to confront Mona publicly.

7.content: On her first night in Mondstadt Prune covered the city in angry notices against Alice. One at Millhaven, in deep black cursive ink with exclamation points that pierced the paper, denounced the witch "A" as an overgrown toddler who bullies minors and abducted "a vital soul companion (Note: Not just an ordinary pet)". Replies asked her to stop using cursed-looking black ink, passed on Sara's request that she stop occupying a Good Hunter table all afternoon on one drink, and (likely from Kaeya) offered a cavalry-combat permit. Some Mondstadters put up Good Hunter discount coupons beside her posters so the hunter would not go hungry. If the Traveler tears the notice down, she wonders whether a witch's minion did it.

8.content: Prune's parents, Mondstadters lured abroad by sayings like "Life is an open road", settled in Nod-Krai: her father worked the docks, her mother held two jobs. They kept her fed and warm but had no time for her, and because Nod-Krai nights were dangerous they kept her home. She read daily at Mimisbrunnr Books, whose owner was too busy selling investment coupons to wealthy clients to mind her, and liked to tuck herself into cozy corners of Nasha Town to read and watch people, noting that the rules in books never change while people keep breaking them. She once proudly found that her mother had been shortchanged three days' pay. She hid her fear of the dark and her wish for a Mondstadt pinwheel to spare her parents guilt.

9.content: Prune wanted an Electro Vision: cold and swift, the right element to strike a witch, and conveniently purple to match her black-and-metal wardrobe. She read the Spantamad guide to elemental power three times and memorised everything on Electro. Then, unable to lift her over-modified hammer, she gave in and recited a fairy-tale incantation in private, eyes squeezed shut ("O Hexhunter Oathhammer... UNLEASH!!!"). The hammer turned light as a feather and a Vision dropped into her palm: Anemo. She yelled at the sky that she had studied for Electro, then wiped the Vision clean and resolved to study the Anemo chapters and use the wind to scatter the witch's traps.

10.content: Prune met the three in the limited-time Phantasmal Pals event. Yaoyao, dutiful and kind, often ties Prune's hair ribbon and once let her nap on her shoulder because "everyone has weaknesses they don't want others to see". Qiqi, who loves Dango Milk from the tea party, received a book on finches and a heap of buy-one-get-one-free Dango Milk; she says Prune looks tough but has soft palms. Prune approves of Sayu sleeping "while she still can", gave her "An Introduction to Nutrition" to help her grow, and taught her hammer stilts; Sayu notes that they are still the same height.

11.content: Albedo, Klee's guardian, collected Prune from the Knights after the Mona incident and picks Klee up after their play dates. Prune visits him with questions about the "nature of being"; their talks end when he poses counter-questions, but she always comes back with a notebook full of answers, which pleases him. She confides to the Traveler that she suspects he is not human, because nobody could be that perfect.
